- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes followed by rapid declines, model tends to overshoot downward — adjust forecast to be 1–3% less aggressive in decline.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is consistently below true outcome, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (especially in first 5–7 days), model exhibits lag — adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome across multiple periods, consider mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive and forecast is high, model overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with historical mean.  
- If forecast is below true outcome and sentiment is negative, model is underreacting — increase forecast by 1–3% to reflect sentiment shift.
